concerns.text: T014 ('Implement recovery segment tagging logic... using... attention-weighted overlap') contradicts the data-flow dependency established in T006 and the Plan's 'Complexity Tracking' (which explicitly forbids model attention to avoid circularity). T014 attempts to consume a 'model attention' artifact that the foundational tasks (T006) and plan explicitly declare non-existent. This creates a semantic ordering violation where a consumer task relies on a producer that is forbidden by the spec.

T023 ('Execute agent... under Binary, 3-Bin, and Random Pruning conditions') conflates the execution of the experimental variable (fidelity) with the control condition (Random Pruning). Per FR-009, Random Pruning is a control independent of reward signals. T023 implies a single execution pass handles both, risking a hidden dependency where the random pruning logic is not isolated from the fidelity-driven pruning logic defined in T020/T021. The task order should separate the 'Random Pruning' execution into its own distinct task to ensure the control condition is produced independently before analysis.

T024 and T025 are listed under 'Implementation for User Story 2' but share IDs with T024/T025 in 'Tests for User Story 3'. This ID collision breaks the deterministic ordering and traceability of the task list. T024 (US2) and T024 (US3) cannot be distinguished in the execution order.

T010 and T011 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but are contract/integration tests for US1. While they may run in parallel, they depend on the *completion* of T012 (baseline execution runner) and T014 (tagging logic) to have valid code to test. The [P] tag implies they can run alongside implementation tasks, but the dependency graph requires the implementation to be present first. The [P] tag is misleading here; they should be ordered after the implementation tasks they test, or the [P] tag should be removed to reflect the sequential dependency on code existence.
